message.content:
Here’s a quick example (Python) that shows how to pull all DNS records for **sample.com**, filter out the CNAME entries, and print only their object IDs:

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "secret123"          # <-- your key
DOMAIN    = "sample.com"
BASE_URL  = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/dns_records"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
}

response = requests.get(BASE_URL, headers=headers)
data     = response.json()

# Each record is under data[*]
for rec in data.get("data", []):
    if rec.get("attributes", {}).get("record_type") == "CNAME":
        print(rec["id"])
```

If you prefer `curl`, the equivalent command is:

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: secret123" \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records
```

…and then parse the JSON to extract the `"id"` fields where `"record_type":"CNAME"`.

That will give you a list of the object IDs for all CNAME records associated with *sample.com*.
